baselineSelector.mechanism: Build time. src/shared/lib/state/backend.ts, src/features/preferences/index.ts and src/features/issue-edit/document.ts each load exactly one implementation via a top-level dynamic import; useLocalState in src/shared/lib/state/local.tsx is React useState in the baseline build and the registry binding otherwise. Files with scope baseline-branch are listed, never hidden, but are not bundled in the state-lib build.

categories.app-state: User-visible mutable UI state or async action status owned through useLocalState (registry). Valid runtime-only without any compiler (spec s5-1; owner-supplied s1.13).
categories.opaque-framework-resource: Setter-less React allocation of a controller/registry/scope instance. Content and status live in state-lib stores; React only keeps the instance alive (spec s6-1).
categories.immutable-mount-snapshot: Setter-less value captured once at mount and never changing (password-reset link token).
categories.baseline-selector: The build-time VITE_STATE_BACKEND selection reference to React useState inside the binding.
categories.external-adapter: TanStack Query useQuery/useInfiniteQuery/useMutation: existing server-cache/transport adapter kept as replaceable source/cache (spec s8-1, s8-4). Not a state-lib query engine and not claimed to be one.
categories.baseline-branch: Reference implementation compiled only when VITE_STATE_BACKEND=baseline. It exists for A/B comparison; counted separately.
categories.browser-native: Uncontrolled browser-native widget state (native <details> open flag, defaultValue/defaultChecked inputs). The DOM element owns it; it is counted by the guard, not hidden, and is NOT claimed as state-lib-owned.

Anchor ids and section titles were read (read-only, no network) from a built spec page in a sibling worktree: ../state-toolkit-followups-20261014/ci/site-artifacts/dist-served/spec.html. s1-13 does not exist as an anchor there; section 1.13 could not be located, so it is cited only through /spec#s1.

nonHookOwners.note: Recovery-draft store over browser storage (durable cross-tab copies and per-tab mirror). createDraftPersistence(ports) is a factory: maps, index, revision, listeners, caches and the storage-event subscription belong to the instance and dispose() releases them (late acknowledgements become no-ops). state-lib: DraftPersistenceProvider owns one instance per app mount through a scope (revision = scope value, store = scope resource); there is no module-level fallback in that build. Baseline: lazily built standalone facade over real ports (page-lifetime, as before). Persistence is a source-adapter over browser storage (spec 8.5), not a state-lib persist policy; the store still keeps its own causal-clock/receipt merge instead of state-lib persisters, which is an open gap.

useRef DOM handles, latches and mirrors (locks, current-value mirrors, timers) are not inventoried per site. They hold no rendered state; a user-visible value kept only in a ref would be a defect, and none was found while auditing the files above, but the guard does not check refs.

The settings and knowledge disclosures use Disclosure. state-lib: open is rendered from a registered useLocalState owner and written back from the native toggle event. Baseline keeps the uncontrolled native <details>, the only remaining browser-native site.
Navigation and filter state stays in the URL via the existing router (AGENTS.md); the router is not rewritten and no ownership claim is made for it.

handles.reason: useEphemeralLinkToken reads the reset token from the URL once in a lazy initializer and has no setter; it cannot change after mount, is not user-editable and is not async status. The effect right after it scrubs the token from the address bar, so a mount-lifetime snapshot is the contract. Registering it in the application-wide UI registry would expose a bearer secret to registry inspection with no ownership benefit, so it deliberately stays a React-local immutable snapshot.
